name: NetExplorer
description: Secure cloud file storage and collaboration for NetExplorer tenants, including folders, files, shares, upload links, archives, locks, and trash workflows.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect a NetExplorer tenant with OAuth2 client-credentials (server-to-server) using a tenant base URL plus the tenant-specific client ID and client secret entered in the connection form.
authentication.notes: NetExplorer uses tenant-hosted OAuth2 authorization code flow. Enter the full Platform Base URL without `/api`, then complete the browser sign-in step. This draft freezes the request-time scope to `all` because that is the current explicit authorization-doc contract.

credentials.name: Platform Base URL
credentials.description: The full NetExplorer platform base URL, for example `https://company.netexplorer.pro`. Do not include `/api`.

setupGuide.title: Connect NetExplorer
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a NetExplorer tenant with the Application OAuth2 feature enabled, the full tenant base URL, and a NetExplorer OAuth2 application configured with the Server profile so you can paste its Client ID and Client Secret into the connection form.

steps.title: Open the OAuth2 application settings in your NetExplorer administration
steps.description: Sign in as an administrator, open the administration area, and go to the OAuth2 application configuration screen for your tenant.

steps.title: Create a Server OAuth2 application
steps.description: Create a new OAuth2 application and choose the Server profile so NetExplorer issues an application token instead of asking an end user to approve access.

steps.title: Assign the scopes your automation needs
steps.description: Select only the scopes your workflows need. NetExplorer applies those rights to the application token that will be generated from client_credentials.

steps.title: Copy the tenant URL and OAuth2 credentials into the connection form
steps.description: Paste the full Platform Base URL such as https://company.netexplorer.pro, then paste the Client ID and Client Secret shown by NetExplorer into the connection form. Do not add /api to the Platform Base URL.

steps.title: Copy the values into MindCloud

name: NetLicensing
description: NetLicensing is a license management and software monetization platform for managing products, licensees, licenses, tokens, transactions, bundles, and related licensing resources through a REST API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use NetLicensing API Key Identification. NetLicensing requires HTTP Basic authentication with username `apiKey` and the API key as the password.
authentication.notes: NetLicensing API key authentication is implemented as HTTP Basic authentication with fixed username `apiKey` and the API key as the password. API key role controls which endpoint operations are allowed.

setupGuide.title: Connect NetLicensing
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a NetLicensing vendor account and an API key from the NetLicensing Management Console or token service.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key

steps.title: Connect in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API key into the connection field. MindCloud sends it using NetLicensing API Key Identification over HTTP Basic authentication with username apiKey.

steps.title: Verify the connection

description: Connect to Oracle NetSuite SuiteTalk REST Web Services for core ERP, CRM, sales, purchasing, billing, and lookup records.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect with NetSuite OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant for SuiteTalk REST Web Services.

credentials.name: Account ID
credentials.description: Enter the official NetSuite Account ID from Company Information, for example 123456 for production or 123456_SB1 for sandbox.

credentials.name: Consumer Key / Client ID
credentials.description: Paste the Consumer Key / Client ID shown by NetSuite after saving the OAuth 2.0 integration record.

credentials.name: Consumer Secret / Client Secret
credentials.description: Paste the Consumer Secret / Client Secret shown by NetSuite after saving the OAuth 2.0 integration record. NetSuite only shows this value once.

setupGuide.title: Set up NetSuite OAuth 2.0
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a NetSuite administrator or a role with the Integration Application permission. Use the NetSuite Account ID from Company Information for this connection. Do not copy the NetSuite browser URL or domain as the Account ID.

glossary.definition: The official NetSuite account identifier shown on Company Information, for example 123456 for production or 123456_SB1 for sandbox. Enter this value exactly as NetSuite shows it.
The NetSuite application record that enables OAuth 2.0 and generates the client credentials used by the connection form.
The callback URL shown in the connection form. This is only used when creating the NetSuite OAuth integration record and is not the NetSuite Account ID.

steps.title: Find your NetSuite Account ID
steps.description: Go to Setup > Company > Company Information and copy the Account ID.

steps.title: Create an OAuth 2.0 integration record
steps.description: Go to Setup > Integration > Manage Integrations > New. Enter a name, set State to Enabled, and open the Authentication subtab.

steps.title: Enable the authorization code flow
steps.description: Under OAuth 2.0, check Authorization Code Grant and select the REST Web Services scope. Do not use Client Credentials for this connection.

steps.title: Register the callback URL
steps.description: In Redirect URI, paste the callback URL exactly. Then save the integration record.

steps.title: Copy the generated client credentials
steps.description: After saving, NetSuite shows the generated values once. Paste Consumer Key / Client ID and Consumer Secret / Client Secret into the matching fields in the connection form.

steps.title: Connect NetSuite
steps.description: Return to the connection form, confirm Account ID and the copied OAuth values are filled in, then start the OAuth connection and approve access in NetSuite.

name: NewsBlur
description: NewsBlur is a personal news reader for following RSS feeds, reading unread stories, saving articles, and managing feed subscriptions.

authentication.name: NewsBlur Login
authentication.description: Authenticate to NewsBlur with a username and password. NewsBlur returns session cookies from the login endpoint; subsequent API requests use those cookies.
authentication.notes: NewsBlur API docs state no API key is required, but users must authenticate. Login is POST /api/login with username and password. OAuth exists but requires requesting a client ID and secret from NewsBlur, so this app uses custom cookie-based login.

name: NileDesk
description: No-code BPM platform for process flows, boards, datasets, data forms, and API-driven workflow integrations.

authentication.description: Connect NileDesk with your personal API key and organization ID.

credentials.name: Organization ID

setupGuide.title: Connect NileDesk
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a NileDesk account that can sign in and open the Change Password page in your profile.

steps.title: Enter your organization ID
steps.description: Use the same organization ID you enter when signing in to NileDesk. Paste that value into the Organization ID field in MindCloud.

steps.title: Copy your API key from NileDesk
steps.description: Open your NileDesk profile, open Change Password, and copy your personal API key from that page. Paste it into the API Key field in MindCloud.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, save the connection, and run the test. The connection is ready when the Get Templates action succeeds.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Nimble API token from the Nimble account you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Generate a Nimble API token
steps.description: In Nimble, generate or copy the API token for the account you want to connect.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Use that token as the app connection API key value. MindCloud will send it as a bearer token when calling Nimble.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.description: Run the connection test to confirm MindCloud can read your Nimble account with the supplied token.

steps.description: Sign in to the NMKR Studio account that owns the projects and NFTs you want MindCloud to access.

steps.description: Enter the API key in the MindCloud test connection. MindCloud sends it as Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>.

name: Novofon

authentication.name: API Key

setupGuide.title: Connect Novofon
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Novofon administrator account with legacy API access enabled. Keep your API Key and API Secret ready before you return to MindCloud.

steps.title: Open the Novofon administrator user settings
steps.description: Sign in to Novofon, open Telephony, then open PBX Users and edit the administrator user.

steps.title: Enable API-key access on the API tab
steps.description: Open the API tab for that administrator user and turn on the option to use an API key.

steps.title: Copy the API Key and API Secret
steps.description: Copy both values from Novofon. You need the API Key and the API Secret because Novofon signs every request.

steps.title: Paste the credentials into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the API Key in the API Key field and the API Secret in the API Secret field, then save the connection.

name: Nvoip
description: Manage Nvoip calls, messages, and verification workflows

authentication.name: Access Token
authentication.description: Use a Nvoip access token as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Generate a Nvoip access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Nvoip account with API access enabled for the primary user.

steps.title: Find your Numbersip (User SIP)
steps.description: In the Nvoip panel, open the user settings area and copy the primary user identifier that ends with 001. Nvoip’s help article describes this as the Numbersip or Usuário SIP used to generate API credentials.

steps.title: Copy your User Token
steps.description: Open the Nvoip API or developer area in the panel and copy the permanent User Token shown there.

steps.title: Generate an access token in Apiary
steps.description: Open the official Nvoip Apiary documentation, go to the OAuth2 authentication section for generating API credentials, leave URI parameters and headers unchanged, and fill the request body with your Numbersip/User SIP and User Token.

steps.title: Copy only the access token value
steps.description: Copy the access_token from the response body. Nvoip documents this token as the credential used in API request headers.

steps.title: Paste the token into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Use the generated access token as the app credential in MindCloud. If the token expires, repeat the same generation flow and replace it.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Use Nyckel OAuth2 client credentials to obtain bearer tokens for protected API requests.

setupGuide.title: Get your Nyckel API credentials

steps.title: Open the Api Keys page

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.description: Copy both values from the Nyckel Security page.

steps.title: Return to MindCloud and enter the credentials
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into this connection and save it so MindCloud can request Nyckel access tokens.

authentication.description: Authenticate Nyne API requests with X-API-Key and X-API-Secret headers.

steps.title: Sign in to Nyne AI

steps.title: Open API Keys
steps.description: Go to https://nyne.ai/api-keys.

steps.title: Create or copy credentials
steps.description: Create an API key if needed, then copy both the API key and API secret.

steps.title: Paste both values into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the API key and API secret fields when creating the MindCloud connection.
